title: Derived cotangent identifications of the three polynomial-pair bar terms
statement:
Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. On the small identity-cover polynomial presentation sites $\mathcal C_1=\mathcal C_{B/A}$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal C_{C/A}$, $\mathcal C_3=\mathcal C_{C/B}$ and pair site $\mathcal E=\mathcal C_{C/B/A}$, put $F_1(P)=\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_P B$, $F_2(Q)=\Omega_{Q/A}\otimes_Q C$, $F_3(S)=\Omega_{S/B}\otimes_S C$, and $M_1=g_1^{-1}F_1\otimes_B C$, $M_2=g_2^{-1}F_2$, $M_3=g_3^{-1}F_3$ as in [lem-trf-cotangent-differential-presheaf-ses]. Write $X_i=K_{\mathcal E}^C(M_i)$ for the category bar complexes [def-trf-derived-colimit-bar-system], regarded in $D(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $c_i$ be the bar reindexing comparisons of [lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek] and $\theta_{T/S}$ the standard cotangent comparisons of [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model]. Each value $F_1(P)$ is a free, hence flat, $B$-module: for $P=A[x_s]$ it is $\bigoplus_s B\,\mathrm dx_s$, and tensoring with this value carries a short exact sequence to its direct sum indexed by $s$. There are canonical isomorphisms in $D(C)$
$$\alpha_1:X_1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C,\qquad\alpha_2:X_2\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{C/A},\qquad\alpha_3:X_3\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{C/B}.$$
Precisely, $\alpha_2=\theta_{C/A}c_2$ and $\alpha_3=\theta_{C/B}c_3$. Under the sectionwise equality $M_1=g_1^{-1}(F_1\otimes_B C)$, $\alpha_1$ is the composite of $c_1(F_1\otimes_B C)$, the flat-presheaf bar-tensor comparison of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-change-rings], and $\theta_{B/A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1$. Its middle comparison identifies $(P_n\to\cdots\to P_0,x\otimes c)$ with $(P_n\to\cdots\to P_0,x)\otimes c$. The target $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$ is represented by the termwise tensor with $C$ of the bounded-above free standard differential complex of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. These assertions hold without flatness of $B\to C$.

source.place: Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), identification of the three terms using Tags 08QW (lemma-triangle-compute-lower-shriek) and 08PU (lemma-compute-cotangent-complex); sites-cohomology Tag 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings), flat-presheaf bar-tensor form.

proof.text: For $P=A[x_s]$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] and extend scalars along $P\to B$. This gives $F_1(P)=\bigoplus_s B\,\mathrm dx_s$, including arbitrary and empty variable sets. Tensoring a short exact sequence with this module gives its direct sum over $s$: injectivity, kernels and surjectivity are checked coordinatewise, with finite support. Thus every value of $F_1$ is flat, with no condition on $B\to C$.

Use the common small skeletons and identity-cover topologies already specified in [lem-trf-cotangent-lower-shriek]. By [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], each $X_i$ represents $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^C M_i$. Precomposition is sectionwise, so at $U$ both $g_1^{-1}(F_1\otimes_B C)$ and $M_1$ have value $F_1(u_1U)\otimes_B C$ and restriction $F_1(u_1v)\otimes1$ for an arrow $v$. Hence these presheaves agree. The lower-shriek node supplies isomorphisms $c_i(K)$ for every degree-zero coefficient presheaf $K$, with bar representative sending the chain $U_\bullet$ to $u_iU_\bullet$ and retaining its coefficient.

source.place: Tag 08QW (lemma-triangle-compute-lower-shriek); sites-cohomology Tags 08PG/08PH (derived colimit bar model and reindexing).

proof.text: Apply the preceding comparisons over the constant coefficient ring $C$ to $K=F_2$ and $K=F_3$. They give $X_2\simeq L\pi_{2,!}^C F_2$ and $X_3\simeq L\pi_{3,!}^C F_3$. Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model] to the ring maps $A\to C$ and $B\to C$. Its canonical isomorphisms have precisely these sources and targets $L_{C/A}$ and $L_{C/B}$. Their composites are therefore the specified $\alpha_2=\theta_{C/A}c_2(F_2)$ and $\alpha_3=\theta_{C/B}c_3(F_3)$.

source.place: Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), second and third terms; Tags 08QW and 08PU.

proof.text: For the first term apply $c_1$ over $C$ to $F_1\otimes_B C$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-colimit-change-rings] on $\mathcal C_1$ with $R=B$, $S=C$, $F=F_1$. The flat-value hypothesis was proved in Step 1, and $F_1[0]$ is bounded above. Thus its flat-presheaf comparison identifies $L\pi_{1,!}^C(F_1\otimes_B C)$ with $(L\pi_{1,!}^B F_1)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$. Follow it by the image of $\theta_{B/A}$ from [lem-trf-cotangent-sheaf-model] under derived extension of scalars. This defines $\alpha_1$ as the required composite of isomorphisms. The change-of-rings node gives exactly $(P_n\to\cdots\to P_0,x\otimes c)\leftrightarrow(P_n\to\cdots\to P_0,x)\otimes c$ for its middle map and expressly imposes no flatness on $C$ over $B$.

source.place: Tag 08QX (proposition-triangle), first term; sites-cohomology Tag 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings), flat-presheaf bar form.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], $L_{B/A}$ is represented by $D=s(\Omega^1_{P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet}B)$, zero in positive degrees. Every $P^{\mathrm{std}}_n$ is polynomial over $A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] makes $D^{-n}=F_1(P^{\mathrm{std}}_n\to B)$ free over $B$; Step 1 proves its flatness. Let $\mathcal T$ be the one-object site whose only covering sieve is the maximal one; it is small in the chosen coefficient universe. By [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification], evaluation identifies $\underline B$-module sheaves with $B$-modules, sheaf tensor with ordinary tensor (so the terms of $D$ stay flat), K-flat complexes with K-flat complexes, and $D(\underline B),D(\underline C)$ with $D(B),D(C)$; it turns the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] along $\underline B\to\underline C$ into the ordinary derived scalar extension $-\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$ used in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-change-rings], with the same resolution computation isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] on $\mathcal T$ with ring $\underline B$: $D$ is K-flat. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], clause (2), on $\mathcal T$ with $B\to C$ and the identity resolution $D\to D$. It represents $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$ by the termwise tensor $D\otimes_B C$, as asserted. All three comparisons above use the canonical maps supplied by their cited statements; composition and applying the derived scalar-extension functor preserve isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), specialized to the point; derived change of rings by K-flat models. Cotangent Tags 08PN/08PU identify the standard model.
